minutes.headline: Commissioners voted on new water rate tiers for heavy usage, and discussed GIS mapping, lead-line rules, a cyber grant and CDL training.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners signed warrants, approved the October 26th minutes (deferring October 19th), and moved to approve two new higher-usage rate blocks. The superintendent's report covered GIS mapping, the state lead and copper revision, a garage roof repair, a truck replacement bid, a cyber security grant, and in-house CDL training. A Woodlands resident delivered concerns for the well pilot study and asked about minutes, agendas and the rate chart.

public_comment.topic: A Woodlands resident, newly named Woodlands representative for the well pilot study, handed in written concerns from the trustees for the water district and its engineers to consider before next week's meeting.
Asked whether meeting minutes and agendas had been published; told a new website link is being created and agendas go on Facebook and the town website.
Asked for a copy of the water usage tier chart; staff read out the new tiers and usage counts.
Said a selectman was appointed to the well pilot study committee; asked about emailing the commissioners.

what_happened.line: Commissioners moved to approve two new higher-usage water rate blocks, blocks two and three; the motion was seconded but the vote count was not audible.
The superintendent said he would meet the cyber vendor and share the scope with a second vendor to prioritize spending of a cyber security grant that was cut roughly in half.
Commissioners approved the October 26th minutes by voice and deferred the October 19th minutes until members have read them.
The superintendent will survey the DPW head and others on need before pursuing in-house CDL training, and will review the sample curriculum.
Minutes are to be posted once a new website link exists; agendas continue on Facebook and the town website.

why_it_matters: The new upper usage blocks change what the heaviest water users pay, so a household's bill depends on which tier its use falls in, and the recording does not confirm the motion passed.
Grant spending, a truck replacement bid and possible CDL training are all costs the district weighs against rates, and residents can follow them only if minutes and agendas are posted.
watch_next: The truck replacement bid opens the week after this meeting; the board can reject bids if the low bid is too high.
The October 19th minutes still await approval, and the Woodlands well pilot study concerns are due to be considered at the next week's meeting.
